svg.text: How ux.md works with the Intent Spec
Two documents, one direction of travel. The gate files hold the reasoning; the Intent Spec holds the conclusion and the signature.
THE REASONING — UNSIGNED, PROVISIONAL ON PURPOSE
ux.md
Gate 1 — do we understand the problem · Gate 2 — is this the right thing
§1 the problem, and for whom
§2 top tasks
§4 THE CONCEPTS — more than one future, side by side
§5 REJECTED AND SUPERSEDED — the forwarding address
## EVIDENCE — which claim rests on which finding
Mandatory. Every project has a problem and some state of knowledge about it.
design.md
Gate 3 — is this one built right
## CONTEXT OF USE — users, tasks, environment (ISO 9241-11)
## EVAL LOOPS — the usability instrument and its threshold
Optional — but a project with no Gate 3 must SAY so. Silence is what's disallowed.
Both are interpretations of the same evidence.
Neither is signed. That is the point: a provisional reading cannot live inside a
signed document without freezing it or devaluing the signature.
THE CONCLUSION — SIGNED, CONTRACTUAL
ACP-HARNESS-INTENT-SPEC.md
Already exists. Already established. Nothing here replaces it.
§5 Requirements — UXI-## · THE SINGLE ID SPACE
§1 desired outcome · success metrics · anti-success signals
§2 why this work exists — the business rationale
§3 users and affected parties
§4 out of scope / non-goals
§7 invariants — FLOOR / FIT split
§12 open questions · §14 testing · §15 evidence requirements
§17 decision log · signatures
The rule, and the reason it matters:
a gate file POINTS at this. It never restates it. Anything written
in both drifts — and the copy in the unsigned document wins by
accident, because it is the one being edited.
A pointer is only honest if the target is filled.
Converting "Direction" to "see §1" is worse than restating it if §1 is a placeholder.
every UXI-## resolves here
one canonical list, not four
direction · non-goals
metrics · decision log
— read from here,
never copied
WHAT TWENTY SECTIONS HAVE NO SLOT FOR — the test of whether the gate files are redundant
1 · Which claim rests on which finding
§2 Source evidence is a source LOG —
one row per document. §15 Evidence
requirements is BUILD verification.
Neither carries a per-claim dependency.
2 · More than one concept
§1 is one outcome statement,
singular and contractual. Five
candidate futures side by side
have nowhere to live.
3 · A forwarding address
§17 logs decisions taken. §12
logs questions open. Neither
holds this was a contender, and
4 · The marked leap
Nothing in §0–§20 separates
"this is a finding" from "this is
our reading of one." A contract
asserts — that is its job.
Everything else a gate file might hold is already in the Intent Spec, and belongs there. Six of the fourteen sections originally proposed became pointers.
Beth Connor · 2026-09-22 · ux.md holds Gates 1 and 2 since the vision.md merge; project.conf points GATE_1 and GATE_2 at the same file and check-gates.sh dedupes.
Spec-driven tooling and the Intent Spec were both written for code. A code spec may assume itself correct and check the build against it; a claim about people may not.
